newsitem.title: USA: Unocal reports lower 2nd quarter operating profit.
newsitem.headline: Unocal reports lower 2nd quarter operating profit.

text.p: Unocal Corp Wednesday reported weaker than expected second quarter operating profits, reflecting lower worldwide crude oil prices and domestic natural gas prices, and higher international exploration expenses.

In a statement, the oil company said earnings from continuing operations, excluding one-time items, totaled $97 million or 39 cents a share in the three months ended in June, down from $157 million or 60 cents a year ago. The quarterly profit was below Wall Street's consensus estimate of 45 cents a share.

Including one time items in both the current period and the year-ago period, Unocal reported second quarter net income of $118 million, or 48 cents a share, compared with $238 million, or 92 cents per common share, for the same period a year ago.

The most recent quarter included an after-tax gain of $41 million from the sale of Unocal Hydrocarbon Sales to a U.S. affiliate of Petroleos de Venezuela, S.A. (PDVSA), an after-tax gain of $39 million resulting from the May restructuring of The UNO-VEN Co., and a charge of $38 million for the early extinguishment of debt.

"While we had hoped for more encouraging results from Perdana Deep-1, we remain excited about oil and gas prospects in this historically prolific resource area," said Roger Beach, Unocal chairman and chief executive officer.Beach. "We've only just begun to explore Blocks A and C/D. Perdana Deep-1, which was spudded before we farmed in to the project, was only the first well drilled in this 600,000-acre area."
The company also recorded a $7 million charge relating to a June blow-out of the Moulavi Bazar No. 1 exploration well in northeast Bangladesh.
"Higher Far East production and reduced interest expense partially offset higher dry hole costs and lower oil and gas prices," said Roger Beach, Unocal chairman and chief executive officer.
Natural gas production in the Far East was up 26 percent, or 161 million cubic feet (mmcf) per day, over the second quarter 1996.

Domestic natural gas production averaged 1,001 million cubic feet per day (mmcf) per day, down 52 mmcf compared with the second quarter 1996. Crude oil and condensate production decreased to 77,300 barrels per day compared with 88,500 barrels for the second quarter last year. These decreases were attributed to natural production declines and maintenance-related platform shut-ins in the U.S. Gulf of Mexico.

Worldwide, Unocal's average sales price for crude and condensate was $17.28 per barrel, compared with $18.71 in the second quarter 1996, while the sales price for natural gas averaged $2.06 per thousand cubic feet, compared with $2.15 for the same period last year.
Unocal shares were off 25 cents to $38.675 in New York Stock Exchange trading.
